mainTopic: Can a son collect a debt by oath when his father would have needed an oath? The challenge to רב ושמואל's rule (אין אדם מוריש שבועה לבניו), רב יוסף's answer, and רב נחמן's decision to limit the rule.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא that seems to contradict רב ושמואל. Their rule is that a father cannot pass down to his son an oath he would have had to take. רב יוסף answers that the ברייתא follows בית שמאי. רב נחמן refuses to overturn רב ושמואל, but he rules that their rule should not be extended. Two attempts to treat a case as outside the rule are rejected: a guarantor, and a brother as heir. רב חמא says the הלכה was never decided between רב ושמואל and רבי אלעזר, so a judge who follows either one has ruled properly. רב פפא therefore says an orphans' document is neither torn up nor used to collect. The גמרא then explains the משנה: partners, sharecroppers and a household manager swear even on a 'maybe' claim, because they tend to allow themselves to take. That oath requires a denied claim worth two silver מעה, like רב. Finally, a ברייתא about שביעית proves that other claims can be rolled onto a rabbinic oath. The amud ends as רב הונא begins a new statement.

steps.title: The ברייתא: The Son Can Be Stronger Than the Father
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a son can collect with or without an oath, while the father collects only with an oath. The גמרא identifies the case as one where the borrower died during the lender's lifetime.
steps.simpleTranslation: The son can collect either with an oath or without one, but the father can collect only with an oath. What is the case? The borrower died while the lender was still alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא and pins down which case it is talking about. This sets up a challenge to רב ושמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the borrower dies, the lender (the father) must swear before collecting from the borrower's orphans. רב ושמואל said that if the father then dies, his son cannot collect, because a person cannot pass down an oath to his children. This ברייתא seems to describe exactly that case.

keyTerms.meaning: collects (a debt)
an oath
the borrower
the lender
what is the case? (asks for the exact situation)

phrases.english: as the son collects
both with an oath and without an oath,
while the father collects only with an oath.
What is the case?
When the borrower died during the lifetime of the lender.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי – דְּמֵת לֹוֶה בְּחַיֵּי מַלְוֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of a ברייתא brought before this point to challenge רב ושמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ושמואל's rule that a person cannot pass down an oath to his children.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It sets up the case of the borrower dying first, which is exactly the case where רב ושמואל's rule applies.

steps.title: The Contradiction to רב ושמואל Is Spelled Out
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the son collects with an oath, meaning the heirs' oath. That suggests the son can collect even though his father needed an oath, which contradicts רב ושמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the ברייתא teaches that the son collects both with and without an oath. 'With an oath' means the heirs' oath. 'Without an oath' follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who rules that way when witnesses report the father's dying words. This contradicts רב ושמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains both halves of the ברייתא and lands the challenge against רב ושמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ordinary case the son collects by taking the heirs' oath (that he does not know of any payment). So a son whose father needed an oath can still collect, which is the opposite of what רב ושמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: and it teaches (introduces the problem in a quoted source)
the heirs' oath: 'our father did not tell us the debt was paid'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the son's oath is the same oath his father would have taken. The son takes a different, weaker oath: the heirs' oath, about what he does not know. The question is whether that is enough to collect.

phrases.english: And it teaches:
that the son collects
both with an oath and without an oath;
'with an oath' means the heirs' oath,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁבוּעָה – כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל!
phrases.english: 'without an oath' follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל!
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה: if witnesses heard the father say before he died that the debt was unpaid, the son collects without swearing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָתָנֵי: שֶׁהַבֵּן גּוֹבֶה בֵּין בִּשְׁבוּעָה וּבֵין שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁבוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the case defined in step 1 to complete the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ושמואל: אין אדם מוריש שבועה לבניו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the case where the father needed an oath, the ברייתא lets the son collect with the heirs' oath. So the son can collect in place of a father who owed an oath.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The ברייתא Follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the ברייתא follows בית שמאי. They hold that a document waiting to be collected counts as if it were already collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Whose view is this? It is בית שמאי, who say that a document standing to be collected is treated as if it were already collected.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends רב ושמואל by saying the ברייתא follows a different view, the view of בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, the debt counts as money the father already had, so the son inherits money, not an oath. רב ושמואל follow the opposite view, so the ברייתא does not refute them.

keyTerms.meaning: whose opinion is this?
the school of שמאי
a document that stands to be collected
is considered as already collected

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge from the ברייתא is answered by saying it follows בית שמאי. רב ושמואל's rule stands for the accepted view.

phrases.english: רב יוסף said:
Whose view is this? It is בית שמאי,
who say:
a document that stands to be collected is considered as already collected.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הָא מַנִּי – בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the source to a different view (בית שמאי).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is the accepted law and shows that a son can collect even when his father needed an oath.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows בית שמאי, who treat the debt as already owned, so the son inherits money rather than an oath. רב ושמואל disagree with that view.

steps.title: A Proposal to Overturn רב ושמואל
steps.stepSummary: When רב נחמן comes to סורא, רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא suggest overturning רב ושמואל's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן happened to come to סורא. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא went in to see him and said: Let the Master come, and we will uproot that ruling of רב ושמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. Two sages propose canceling רב ושמואל's rule, which sets up רב נחמן's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after רב יוסף's defense, these sages still find the rule hard to accept. They want an important judge like רב נחמן to join them in rejecting it.

keyTerms.meaning: happened to arrive
the city of סורא, home of a great academy
let us uproot it

phrases.english: רב נחמן happened to come to סורא;

phrases.aramaic: עוּל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא went in to him,
they said to him:
Let the Master come
and let us uproot that ruling of רב ושמואל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the defense of רב ושמואל, a story shows sages wanting to overturn the rule anyway.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposal: overturn רב ושמואל's rule that a person cannot pass down an oath to his children.

steps.title: רב נחמן: Don't Uproot It, Just Don't Extend It
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן refuses to cancel רב ושמואל's ruling but agrees not to apply it to any new cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Did I trouble myself and travel all these parasangs just to uproot the ruling of רב ושמואל?! Rather, let us not add to it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rejects the proposal to overturn the rule. He decides instead to keep it limited to its own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן respects רב ושמואל too much to cancel their ruling. Because the rule is hard to accept, though, it should not be stretched beyond the case they actually ruled on: a borrower who died in the lender's lifetime.

keyTerms.meaning: I troubled myself, made the effort
parasangs (a long distance measure)
let us not add to it (don't extend the rule)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the approach for the rest of the sugya: רב ושמואל's rule stays, but only in its original case.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Did I trouble myself and come all these parasangs,
to uproot that ruling of רב ושמואל?!
Rather, let us not add to it;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the proposal in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב ושמואל's rule is kept but not extended to other situations.

steps.title: Example: רב פפא's Case of a Weakened Document
steps.stepSummary: As an example of not extending the rule, רב פפא rules that when a lender weakens his own document and then dies, his heirs take the heirs' oath and collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, what רב פפא said: if someone weakens his own document and dies, the heirs take the heirs' oath and collect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an example of a case where רב ושמואל's rule is not stretched, so the heirs still collect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father had to swear because he admitted to partial payment, not because the borrower died. Since this is not the original case of רב ושמואל, the heirs may collect with the heirs' oath.

keyTerms.meaning: for example
one who weakens his own document (by admitting partial payment)
they take (collect)

steps.whatToRemember: רב ושמואל's rule applies only when the father's oath came about because the borrower died. In other cases, like a weakened document, the heirs swear the heirs' oath and collect.

phrases.english: For example, what רב פפא said:
one who weakens his document and dies:
phrases.notes: He weakens it by admitting he already got part of the money, so he has to swear before collecting the rest.

phrases.english: the heirs swear the heirs' oath,
and collect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates step 5's principle of not extending רב ושמואל's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a lender weakens his document and dies, his heirs take the heirs' oath and collect.

steps.title: The case of a borrower who died and left a guarantor
steps.stepSummary: A borrower died and left a guarantor. רב פפא wanted to say this is another case where רב ושמואל's ruling should not be extended.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who died and left a guarantor. רב פפא wanted to say: this too is a case where we should not extend the rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case and tells us what רב פפא first thought. This sets up the next step, where his idea will be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ושמואל's rule is about heirs collecting from orphans. Here the lender's heirs want to collect from the guarantor, who is not an orphan. רב פפא thought that since this case is different, the rule should not be stretched to cover it, just like in his ruling in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantor, someone who promised to pay if the borrower does not
Died
He thought to say (a first idea that may be rejected)
We should not add onto it, meaning not extend the rule to new cases

phrases.english: There was a certain man who died and left a guarantor.
phrases.notes: The one who died is the borrower. The lender's heirs now want to collect from the guarantor.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa thought to say:

phrases.aramaic: הָא נָמֵי – דְּלָא לוֹסֵיף עֲלַהּ הוּא.
phrases.english: This too is a case where we should not extend the rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דִּשְׁכֵיב, וּשְׁבַק עָרְבָא. סְבַר רַב פָּפָּא לְמֵימָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second application of רב נחמן's instruction not to extend רב ושמואל's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First thought: collecting from a guarantor is outside רב ושמואל's rule, so the heirs could collect.

steps.title: The guarantor will go after the orphans anyway
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rejects רב פפא's idea: the guarantor will go collect from the orphans, so in the end it is the same as collecting from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said to רב פפא: Isn't it true that the guarantor will go after the orphans?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא's first thought is pushed away. Collecting from the guarantor is really collecting from the orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the guarantor pays, he will turn around and collect from the borrower's orphans. So the orphans end up paying a debt that the heirs could not have collected from them directly. That means this case is the same as רב ושמואל's case and is not a new case.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say…? (a challenging question)
Orphans
After
Goes

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the guarantor is the same person as the orphans. The point is that the money comes from the orphans in the end, so the guarantor case is not really new.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said to Rav Pappa:

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ עָרְבָא לָאו בָּתַר יַתְמֵי אָזֵיל?!
phrases.english: Is that to say the guarantor will not go after the orphans?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא: אַטּוּ עָרְבָא לָאו בָּתַר יַתְמֵי אָזֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's proposed distinction
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects treating the guarantor case as a new case outside רב ושמואל's rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores that the guarantor will collect from the orphans, so they pay in the end

steps.title: The case of a lender who died and left a brother
steps.stepSummary: A lender died and left a brother as his heir. רמי בר חמא wanted to say this too is a case where the rule should not be extended.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who died and left a brother. רמי בר חמא wanted to say: this too is a case where we should not extend the rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case and tells us רמי בר חמא's first thought. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ושמואל spoke about a son inheriting from his father. Here the heir is a brother. רמי בר חמא thought that since the case was not mentioned, the brother could collect.

keyTerms.meaning: A brother
Left behind

phrases.english: There was a certain man who died and left a brother.
phrases.notes: Here the one who died is the lender, and his brother inherits him.

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama thought to say:

phrases.aramaic: הָא נָמֵי – דְּלָא לוֹסֵיף עֲלַהּ הוּא.
phrases.english: This too is a case where we should not extend the rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דִּשְׁכֵיב, וּשְׁבַק אַחָא. סָבַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another attempt to limit רב ושמואל's rule, with the same pattern as step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First thought: a brother as heir is outside רב ושמואל's rule, so he could collect.

steps.title: Father or brother makes no difference
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the distinction: the heir's oath is the same whether he says 'my father did not tell me' or 'my brother did not tell me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: What difference is it to me if he swears 'My father did not tell me' or 'My brother did not tell me'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes away רמי בר חמא's idea. A brother is just like a son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem in רב ושמואל's rule is the kind of oath the heir can take. Any heir can only swear he was not told the debt was paid. Whether the one who died was his father or his brother does not change that, so the brother is included in the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference is it to me (there is no difference)
Told me, instructed me

steps.whatToRemember: Not extending רב ושמואל's rule applies only to a truly new case. The guarantor case and the brother case are really the same as the original case, so the rule applies to them.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
What difference is it to me if he swears 'My father did not tell me,'
phrases.notes: These are the words of the heirs' oath: 'I was not told the debt was paid.'

phrases.english: or if he swears 'My brother did not tell me.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: מָה לִי שֶׁלֹּא פְּקָדַנִי אַבָּא, וּמָה לִי שֶׁלֹּא פְּקָדַנִי אָחִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רמי בר חמא's proposed distinction
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects treating a brother as heir as a new case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The heir's oath is the same whether the one who died was his father or his brother

steps.title: A judge may follow either opinion
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא says that since no הלכה was stated like רב ושמואל or like רבי אלעזר, a judge who follows either one has ruled properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא said: Since the הלכה was not stated like רב ושמואל or like רבי אלעזר, a judge who ruled like רב ושמואל has ruled, and one who ruled like רבי אלעזר has ruled.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא steps back and tells us the dispute was never decided, so either ruling is valid. This sets up רב פפא's practical rule in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ושמואל say the heirs cannot collect, and רבי אלעזר disagrees and lets them collect. Since no final ruling was made, a judge who follows either side is not making a mistake, and his ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The final law
A judge
He did, meaning his ruling stands

phrases.english: Rav Ḥama said:
Now that the halakha was not stated

phrases.aramaic: לָא כְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל וְלָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר;
phrases.english: not like Rav and Shmuel and not like Rabbi Elazar,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי דַּיָּינָא דַּעֲבַד כְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל – עֲבַד,
phrases.english: a judge who ruled like Rav and Shmuel has ruled,
phrases.notes: 'Has ruled' means his ruling stands and is not reversed.

phrases.english: and one who ruled like Rabbi Elazar has ruled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָמָא: הַשְׁתָּא דְּלָא אִיתְּמַר הִלְכְתָא לָא כְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל וְלָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from specific cases to the overall status of the dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the הלכה is undecided, a judge's ruling following either רב ושמואל or רבי אלעזר stands.

steps.title: The orphans' document is neither torn nor used to collect
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that the orphans' document is not torn up and not used to collect. We don't collect in case the הלכה follows רב ושמואל, and we don't tear it because a judge who follows רבי אלעזר has ruled properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The orphans' document is not torn up, and we do not collect with it. We don't collect with it because maybe we hold like רב ושמואל. We don't tear it up because a judge who rules like רבי אלעזר has ruled properly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the practical bottom line for a בית דין: leave the document as it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since either side might be right, the בית דין does not act on its own. Collecting could be wrong if רב ושמואל are right. Tearing the document would destroy the orphans' rights, even though another judge could properly let them collect like רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A document, here a loan document
We tear up (to cancel the document)
We collect (the court helps collect with it)
Perhaps

steps.whatToRemember: Bottom line: רב ושמואל's rule is kept but not extended, the הלכה between them and רבי אלעזר is undecided, and so the orphans' document is neither collected nor torn up.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a בית דין acts when a dispute is undecided: it does not act on either side and leaves the document as it is.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This document of orphans,
phrases.notes: A loan document the orphans inherited, where their father would have needed an oath to collect.

phrases.english: we do not tear it up,
and we do not collect with it.
We do not collect with it
because perhaps we hold like Rav and Shmuel;
and we do not tear it up

phrases.aramaic: דְּהַאי דַּיָּינָא דַּעֲבַד כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, עֲבַד.
phrases.english: because a judge who rules like Rabbi Elazar has ruled properly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַאי שְׁטָרָא דְּיַתְמֵי לָא מִקְרָע קָרְעִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רב חמא's statement into a practical rule for the court
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The orphans' document is left as it is: not torn up, and not used to collect.

steps.title: A judge rules like רבי אלעזר and a scholar objects
steps.stepSummary: A judge ruled like רבי אלעזר. A young scholar in his town threatened to bring a letter from ארץ ישראל saying the הלכה is not like רבי אלעזר. The judge answered: 'When you bring it, we'll see.'
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a judge who ruled like רבי אלעזר. A young Torah scholar in his town said to him: 'I will bring a letter from ארץ ישראל saying the הלכה is not like רבי אלעזר.' The judge said: 'When you bring it, we'll talk.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. This step sets the scene for רב חמא's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real-life test of רב חמא's rule from Step 11. The scholar is challenging the judge's ruling with a threat of outside proof. The judge does not back down because of a letter that has not arrived yet.

keyTerms.meaning: a judge
a young Torah scholar
a letter
'the West', meaning ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: There was a certain judge who ruled like Rabbi Elazar.
There was a young Torah scholar in his town.
He said to him: I will bring a letter from the West
phrases.notes: 'The West' is how the בבלי refers to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: saying that the halacha is not like Rabbi Elazar.
He said to him: When you bring it, then we'll see.
phrases.notes: The judge means: until that letter actually shows up, my ruling stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a story that illustrates רב חמא's rule, which Step 12 relied on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge ruled like רבי אלעזר and refused to change his ruling because of a letter that had only been threatened.

steps.title: רב חמא backs the judge's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The scholar went to רב חמא. רב חמא said that a judge who ruled like רבי אלעזר has ruled, and the ruling stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The scholar came before רב חמא. רב חמא said: 'A judge who ruled like רבי אלעזר has ruled.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא settles the story by upholding the judge's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This puts רב חמא's principle from Step 11 into practice. No final הלכה was set either way, so a ruling that follows רבי אלעזר is valid and is not undone.

keyTerms.meaning: 'he did', meaning his ruling is done and stands

steps.whatToRemember: When the הלכה was never decided between רב ושמואל and רבי אלעזר, a judge who ruled like either one has ruled properly. His ruling stays, and so we also don't tear up the orphans' document.

phrases.english: He came before Rav Chama.
He said to him: This judge,
who ruled like Rabbi Elazar, has ruled.
phrases.notes: In other words, what he did is done, and his ruling isn't overturned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story from Step 13 with רב חמא's decision.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A judge who follows רבי אלעזר has ruled properly, and his ruling cannot be overturned.

steps.title: Would anyone swear when nobody claims anything?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, 'And these take an oath,' and asks: are we talking about fools who swear when no one has made a claim against them?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'And these people take an oath.' Are we dealing with fools?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the next line of the משנה and points out that the wording sounds strange.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the משנה sounds like these people swear even with no claim at all. That makes no sense, because no sane person takes an oath when nobody is asking for anything.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and these take an oath', the opening words of the משנה
'is that to say...?', a word that opens a puzzled challenge
fools

phrases.english: And these take an oath.
Is that to say we are dealing with fools?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the orphans' document topic and moves on to a new section of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה means they swear without any claim at all, it describes fools, since nobody swears for no reason.

steps.title: They swear even on an 'I'm not sure' claim
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means that these people must swear even when the claim against them is only a טענת שמא (an uncertain claim) and not a טענת ברי (a definite claim). Examples are partners and sharecroppers.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: these people swear even when the claim against them is not a sure claim but only an 'I'm not sure' claim. For example, partners and sharecroppers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the משנה really means, which answers the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a claim after all, but it is a weak one: 'maybe you took something.' Normally a שמא claim does not create an oath. For these people, though, it does.

keyTerms.meaning: 'this is what it means', used to explain a source's wording
a definite claim ('I'm sure you owe me')
an uncertain claim ('maybe you owe me')
partners
sharecroppers

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the answer as 'no claim at all.' There IS a claim. It is just a שמא claim, which usually would not be enough to require an oath.

phrases.english: This is what it means: And these take an oath
not on a definite claim
but on an uncertain claim:
partners and sharecroppers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say they swear with no claim at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: They swear even when the claim is only a טענת שמא.

steps.title: Who counts as a בן בית
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines the משנה's בן בית. It is not just someone who comes and goes in the house. It is someone who actually manages it: he hires and lets go of workers and brings produce in and sends it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: the בן בית the משנה mentions is not someone who just walks in and out of the house. He is someone who brings in workers and sends out workers, and brings in produce and sends out produce for the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to define one of the people on the משנה's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a real manager who handles the household's money and goods falls under this oath. A friend or visitor who is often in the house does not.

keyTerms.meaning: a household member who manages the house's affairs
workers
produce

phrases.english: It was taught: The household member they mentioned
is not one who just goes in and out on his feet,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מַכְנִיס לוֹ פּוֹעֲלִין וּמוֹצִיא לוֹ פּוֹעֲלִין,
phrases.english: but rather one who brings in workers for him and sends out workers for him,

phrases.aramaic: מַכְנִיס לוֹ פֵּירוֹת וּמוֹצִיא לוֹ פֵּירוֹת.
phrases.english: brings in produce for him and sends out produce for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines one of the people in the משנה's list explained in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בן בית in the משנה is someone who actively manages the household's workers and produce.

steps.title: Why are these people different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why these people have to swear on a שמא claim when others do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about these people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a 'maybe' claim does not obligate anyone to swear. So something about these people must explain why they are treated more strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: 'what is different?', a request for the reason behind a distinction

phrases.english: And what is different about these?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule explained in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why partners, sharecroppers and the others must swear even on a טענת שמא.

steps.title: They tend to allow themselves to take
steps.stepSummary: These people tend to feel it is permitted for them to take some of what they manage. So even a 'maybe' claim is taken seriously.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they allow themselves to take from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question and gives the reason for the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A manager or partner may tell himself that he has a right to take a little for himself. Because of that, there is a real chance he took something, so a שמא claim is enough to make him swear.

keyTerms.meaning: they rule for themselves that it is permitted (to take from it)

steps.whatToRemember: Partners, sharecroppers, managers and the like must swear even on a 'maybe' claim, because people in these roles tend to allow themselves to take from what they handle.

phrases.english: Because they rule for themselves that it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They tend to allow themselves to take from the property they handle, so even a שמא claim is likely enough to require an oath.

steps.title: The oath needs a claim worth two silver coins
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the partner or sharecropper only swears on a 'maybe' claim if the claim is worth at least שתי כסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: These people only have to swear when the claim between them is worth at least two silver מעה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds a limit to the oath of partners and sharecroppers. A tiny claim is not enough. It must be worth at least two silver מעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 16-19 taught that these people swear even on a טענת שמא. Now רב נחמן puts a minimum value on that oath. Below שתי כסף, there is no oath.

keyTerms.meaning: A claim one side makes against the other
Two silver מעה, the smallest amount that can bring an oath
'And that is only when', a phrase that adds a condition

phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said
that Rav Nachman said:
And that is only when there is a claim between them
phrases.notes: 'That' means the 'maybe' oath of partners, sharecroppers and the household manager from the משנה.

phrases.english: of two silver [ma'a].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a minimum value to the שמא oath explained in steps 16-19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The partner's or sharecropper's oath applies only when the claim is worth at least שתי כסף

steps.title: Does this follow שמואל against רב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב נחמן's ruling follows שמואל. That seems hard, because רבי חייא taught a ברייתא that supports רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? Is it שמואל's? But רבי חייא taught a ברייתא that supports רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which opinion רב נחמן's 'two silver' rule follows. It worries that the rule matches שמואל, even though a ברייתא backs רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (39b), רב and שמואל argued about where the two מעה must be. שמואל said the whole claim must be worth two מעה. רב said the part that is denied must be worth two מעה. 'A claim between them of two silver' sounds like the whole claim, which is שמואל's view. But רבי חייא's ברייתא supports רב, so why rule like שמואל?

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like whom?', asking which opinion a ruling follows
'But didn't [he] teach', introducing a ברייתא as a challenge
To support him

phrases.english: Like whom? Like Shmuel?!
phrases.notes: שמואל counts the whole claim toward the two מעה. רב counts only the part being denied.

phrases.english: But Rabbi Chiya taught [a baraita]
in support of Rav!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רב נחמן's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's phrase 'a claim between them of two silver'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase sounds like the whole claim, which is שמואל's view. But a ברייתא supports רב, so the ruling should not follow שמואל.

steps.title: Read it as the denied part, like רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן means the denied part of the claim must be worth two מעה, just as רב holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that he means the denial of the claim must be worth two מעה, like רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads רב נחמן's words. The two silver מעה refer to the part that is denied, so the ruling follows רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one's opinion changes here. Only the reading of רב נחמן's words changes. 'A claim of two silver' now means a denial worth two silver, so the ruling fits the ברייתא that supports רב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say', used to read a statement in a different way
The denial of a claim, meaning the part the defendant says he does not owe

steps.whatToRemember: The two silver מעה in רב נחמן's rule are measured by the denied part, like רב.

phrases.english: Say: [two silver of] the denial of the claim,
like Rav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'A claim between them' meant the whole claim, like שמואל
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the denied part, like רב

steps.title: Can a rabbinic oath carry other claims along with it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about partners who already divided. Then it asks whether גלגול works when the first oath is only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: once the partners and sharecroppers have divided, the oath no longer applies. A question was asked: may one roll other claims onto an oath that is only rabbinic?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה about partners who have divided. It uses that line to set up a new question about גלגול שבועה with a rabbinic oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גלגול means that once a person must swear, the other side can add more claims to the same oath. That claims would not bring an oath on their own. The partners' oath on a 'maybe' claim is only rabbinic. So the question is whether a rabbinic oath is strong enough to carry other claims.

keyTerms.meaning: They divided the shared property
Partners and sharecroppers
'A question was asked of them', an open question of the Sages
To 'roll on', adding other claims onto an oath someone already has to take
Rabbinic, not from the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether partners swear. They do, by rabbinic law. The question is whether that rabbinic oath can carry extra claims along with it.

phrases.english: [The משנה says:] If the partners and the sharecroppers divided.
A question was asked of them:
What is the law about rolling on [other claims] with a rabbinic [oath]?
phrases.notes: Rolling on means adding more claims onto an oath the person already has to take.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה and opens a new question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does גלגול שבועה work when the first oath is only rabbinic?

steps.title: A baraita: a loan before שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. Someone borrowed before שביעית and became a partner after it. The lender may not roll the loan onto the partner's oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone borrowed from another before שביעית, and after שביעית he became his partner or sharecropper, the lender may not roll the loan onto his oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question. This step only quotes the case. The proof itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender would like to add the loan to the partner's rabbinic oath. The ברייתא says no. But the reason is not yet clear, and the next step will look at it closely.

keyTerms.meaning: Before the שמיטה year
After the שמיטה year has ended
They do not roll on (other claims)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
[If] he borrowed from him before the Sabbatical Year,
and after the Sabbatical Year
he became his partner or sharecropper,
they do not roll on [the loan to his oath].

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: לָוָה הֵימֶנּוּ עֶרֶב שְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question in step 23
steps.raayaObject: Whether גלגול works with a rabbinic oath
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a loan from before שביעית

steps.title: The inference: in other years, we do roll on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the only reason not to roll on is that שביעית cancelled the loan. In any other year, the loan would be rolled onto the partner's rabbinic oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he may not roll it on is that he borrowed before שביעית, and שביעית came and cancelled the loan. But if he borrowed in the other years of the seven-year cycle, we do roll it on!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at why the ברייתא said 'no'. It shows that the reason is only that the debt was cancelled, so in other years גלגול would work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שביעית wipes out loans, so there is no debt left to swear about. That is the only reason גלגול fails here, not that the oath is rabbinic. So if the loan had not been cancelled, the lender could roll it onto the partner's rabbinic oath. This shows that גלגול works even with a rabbinic oath.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The reason is', used to look closely at why a source rules as it does
It cancelled it (the debt)
'But then', drawing the opposite conclusion from a case
The years of the seven-year שמיטה cycle

steps.whatToRemember: From the ברייתא, the גמרא infers that גלגול works even with a rabbinic oath. It failed only because שביעית had cancelled the debt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that a rabbinic oath, like the partner's oath, can carry other claims along with it, just like a Torah oath.

phrases.english: The reason is that he borrowed from him before the Sabbatical Year,
so the Sabbatical Year came and cancelled it;
but in the other years of the seven-year cycle,
they do roll on!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of the ברייתא quoted in step 24
steps.raayaObject: Whether גלגול works with a rabbinic oath
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from the ברייתא: the only reason given is that שביעית cancelled the loan

steps.title: Maybe the inference points to the reverse case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. Maybe the ברייתא does not teach that a loan is rolled onto a partner's rabbinic oath. Maybe it only teaches the reverse: a partnership from before שביעית is rolled onto a loan oath from after שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't say the lesson is that in the other years of the cycle we roll the loan on. Instead, say the lesson is this: if he became a partner or sharecropper before שביעית and borrowed after שביעית, we roll on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to knock down the proof from the last step. It suggests a different hidden lesson in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the new reading, the loan comes after שביעית, so שביעית does not cancel it, and the loan oath is from the Torah. The partnership claim gets rolled onto that Torah oath. That is rolling onto a Torah oath, so the ברייתא would prove nothing about rolling onto a rabbinic oath.

keyTerms.meaning: The other years of the seven-year cycle
Sharecropper, who works a field for a share of the crop
Before the שביעית year
After the שביעית year has ended
We roll additional claims onto the oath

steps.confusionAlert: The order is flipped here. In this new reading the loan comes after שביעית, so it is not cancelled, and the loan oath is the Torah-level one.

phrases.english: Do not say:
that in the other years of the cycle, we roll it on;
phrases.notes: This is the proof from step 25: in a normal year, the loan would be rolled onto the partner's oath.

phrases.english: rather, say:
if he became his partner or sharecropper
before שביעית,
and after שביעית he borrowed from him,
we roll it on.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא: הָא שְׁאָר שְׁנֵי שָׁבוּעַ – מְגַלְגְּלִין; אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 25 by offering another reading of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that a loan is rolled onto a rabbinic partner oath in a normal year.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's hidden lesson could instead be the reverse case, which involves only rolling onto a Torah oath.

steps.title: The reverse case is already stated openly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the pushback. The reverse case, partnership before שביעית and a loan after it, is already written openly in the ברייתא. So it cannot be the hidden lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that case is taught openly: if he became a partner or sharecropper before שביעית and borrowed after שביעית, we roll it on!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the pushback from step 26. The ברייתא already says that case in so many words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא does not need to hint at something it states outright. So the hint must teach something new. That brings back the original inference: in a normal year, the loan is rolled onto the partner's rabbinic oath.

keyTerms.meaning: Openly, explicitly
It teaches (in the ברייתא)

phrases.english: But it teaches this openly:
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same ברייתא from step 24.

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲשָׂה לוֹ שׁוּתָּף אוֹ אָרִיס עֶרֶב שְׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: if he became his partner or sharecropper before שביעית,
and after שביעית he borrowed from him,
we roll it on!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the alternative reading from step 26 by showing that its case is already stated in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion in step 26 that the ברייתא's hidden lesson is the reverse case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case is stated openly, so reading it as a hint would make the hint pointless.

steps.title: We do roll onto a rabbinic oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that a claim can be rolled onto an oath that is only rabbinic, and it confirms this conclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: we roll claims onto a rabbinic oath! Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question from step 23. גלגול works even when the first oath is rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the alternative reading failed, the original inference stands. A partner's oath is rabbinic, yet a loan claim is rolled onto it. The second שמע מינה confirms the conclusion with no further challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; the conclusion is proven
Rabbinic-level, not from the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: גלגול works even onto a rabbinic oath, like a partner's oath. This is proven from the ברייתא about loans and partnerships around שביעית.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the question from step 23. A rabbinic oath, like the partner's oath on a 'maybe' claim, can carry other claims along with it.

phrases.english: Learn from this: we roll onto a rabbinic oath!
Yes, learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: מְגַלְגְּלִין בִּדְרַבָּנַן! שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion now that the pushback has been removed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Claims are rolled onto an oath even when that oath is only rabbinic.

steps.title: רב הונא begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a statement of רב הונא. His words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up the next move. The גמרא is about to quote a new teaching from רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the attribution appears here. The content of רב הונא's statement comes right after, so this step is just the opening.

phrases.english: Rav Huna says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching after the conclusion in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated; רב הונא's ruling comes on the next amud.
